subject: Evaluation & close cadence: region + serving-mode acceptance criteria
messages:
From: Rajesh Kumar <rajesh.k@medspark.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava@redwood.com>
Cc: engops@medspark.com
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation scope + region question

Ava — thanks for the call this morning. We liked the demo but need to lock two things before we can present to procurement on June 10: 1) a short mutual action plan (MAP) that shows evaluation milestones and acceptance criteria for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private; and 2) confirmation of whether Redwood can commit to US-only data residency during the pilot.

High level ask from my side: can you send a one-page MAP we can share internally (engineering + compliance + procurement) and a lightweight TCO note showing what changes between Hosted/Dedicated/Private for the next 3 months? Also, team needs SOC2 summary and an estimated SLO for 95th percentile latency at 10 qps.

Thanks,
— Rajesh
Medspark — Product Ops
From: Ava Chen <ava@redwood.com>
To: Rajesh Kumar <rajesh.k@medspark.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation scope + region question

Rajesh — great to chat, thanks for the clear asks. Attached is a draft MAP and a short TCO sketch (Medspark_MAP_v1.xlsx). Quick answers up front:

- US-only residency: Yes for Hosted pilot — we can pin the pilot to our US region and restrict logs/storage to US. For Dedicated and Private, residency is customer-controlled (Dedicated in your cloud region or Redwood-managed US pool; Private is your VPC/on-prem).
- 95th pctl latency at 10 qps (text-gen, 2k tokens avg): Hosted (US) ~120–200ms, Dedicated (reserved GPUs, same model) ~80–140ms, Private depends on sizing/quantization — we include recommended sizing in the TCO.

I included a proposed acceptance checklist inside the MAP: functional pass (sample prompts), latency SLA check, security evidence (SOC2 snapshot + architecture diagram), and go/no-go signoffs from EngOps and Procurement. Proposed timeline below — does this align with your June 10 procurement review?

Proposed MAP milestones (high level):
- Week 0 (May 26–30): Kickoff, access, security questionnaire sent.
- Week 1 (Jun 1–6): Pilot runs (Hosted US region), performance baseline + KV/prefix caching enabled.
- Week 2 (Jun 7–13): Validation, procurement packet assembled, final recommendation (hosted vs dedicated vs private).
- Jun 10: Procurement checkpoint — recommendation + commercial ask.

Next steps if that aligns: 1) I'll share the MAP + SOC2 summary; 2) Karthik will follow up on pricing delta for Dedicated/Private; 3) Jonas can run a 24-hour perf run we can hand to EngOps.

Ava
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Rajesh Kumar <rajesh.k@medspark.com>, Ava Chen <ava@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluation scope + region question

Rajesh — following up with the pricing and procurement notes. Attached is the TCO worksheet and a short table of the primary commercial differences. Key bullets:

- Hosted pilot (US region): no upfront commitment, billed usage. For a 3-week pilot at the expected volume we estimate $Xk (see tab Pilot Estimate).
- Dedicated (reserved pool): monthly commit, predictable unit cost ~30–40% lower at steady state; need min 3-month reservation for discounted pricing.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): one-time setup + recurring infra footprint; best for regulated workloads — pricing depends on infra choices and support tier.

Procurement ask we typically see: a pilot PO for Hosted or a committed monthly run rate for Dedicated if you want to avoid pilot overages. If procurement needs a formal commercial terms memo for June 10, we can produce a short SOW + pilot addendum by June 3.

I can also provide draft contract language for data residency and audit rights (we'll include SOC2 artifacts and a runbook for log retention). Let me know what procurement prefers.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference
Attachments: Medspark_MAP_v1.xlsx (worksheet), SOC2-Summary.pdf (attachment stub)
From: Rajesh Kumar <rajesh.k@medspark.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: engops@medspark.com, procurement@medspark.com
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 14:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation scope + region question

Ava / Karthik — this is very helpful. Procurement wants the short SOW + pilot addendum (June 3 deadline) and EngOps asked for a 24-hour perf capture we can run against our sample corpus (privacy-safe subset). Can Jonas run that starting Thursday (Jun 3) and ship the trace + metrics?

Two clarifications from EngOps: 1) for the Hosted pilot, can you confirm that request routing will keep all inference in the US region and that any temporary fallbacks (if the US pool is saturated) will not route to EU/APAC without explicit opt-in? 2) for Dedicated, we need a clear handoff checklist if we move from Hosted to Dedicated mid-pilot.

If you can ship the SOW/pilot addendum and perf run, I think procurement will be ready to route an internal PO for the pilot on Jun 10.

Rgds,
Rajesh
Product Ops — Medspark
